a_n in R, a_n!=0 eventually, L=lim_(n->infinity)|a_(n+1)/a_n|
L<1 => sum |a_n|<infinity
L>1 => a_n does not tend to 0
lim_(n->infinity) n/(n+1) = lim_(n->infinity) (n/(n+1))^2 = 1
sum_(n=1)^infinity 1/n = infinity, sum_(n=1)^infinity 1/n^2 < infinity

x in R
sum_(n=1)^infinity x^n/n converges <=> -1<=x<1
sum_(n=1)^infinity |x^n/n| < infinity <=> |x|<1
x=1 => sum_(n=1)^infinity x^n/n=infinity
|x|>1 => x^n/n does not tend to 0

sum |a_n|<infinity or sum |b_n|<infinity
c_n=sum_(k=0)^n a_k*b_(n-k) => sum_(n=0)^infinity c_n=A*B
